Currently overseeing temple affairs, Ms. Ying (a pseudonym), is a descendant of the Chow family. She revealed to a photojournalist that many years ago, her grandfather, a Tanka fisherman, unexpectedly retrieved a wooden statue of "Fourth Sister" while out at sea. Her grandfather brought the statue home and gave it to the then-young Ms. Ying as a toy; she even sewed clothes for the deity. Unexpectedly, Ms. Ying subsequently developed a high fever and fell ill. Her grandmother received a dream visit from "Seventh Sister," who instructed her grandfather to enshrine the statue in a temple for worship. The Chow family obeyed the divine decree and built the present-day Seventh Sister Temple.

The Seventh Sister Temple is renowned for the efficacy of prayers for romantic luck. Ms. Ying shared a love story. On the evening of the sixth day of the seventh lunar month three years ago, a slightly chubby man with a hint of "baby fat" waited patiently before the temple until midnight on the seventh to pay his respects, and returned the following year to give thanks. Until yesterday evening (the sixth), the man, dressed in red, returned to give thanks holding his girlfriend's hand. Ms. Ying initially did not recognize him, until he smiled somewhat shyly at her while holding his girlfriend's hand, at which point she identified this former discouraged devotee, bearing witness to a romance that has blossomed into fruition.

Speaking about tips for worshipping at the Seventh Sister Temple, Ms. Ying believes that communicating with deities is as simple as having a chat: "Say whatever you want to say, tell Seventh Sister your troubles." If you wish to know Seventh Sister's instructions and the outcome, you can cast divination blocks to seek guidance. During the Qixi festival period, the Seventh Sister Temple is not only a sacred place for seeking love, but also a haven for devotees to unburden their hearts.
